ai_assessment.mitigation_measures:
1. Primary Toe Retention & Arrest (LaRiMiT Cluster 4 / IS:14458 / CEDD Geoguide 1):
   Emergency hydraulic clearance of 365 m³ displaced debris followed by construction of a 20m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H=3.7m, Base=1.85m, Embedment=1.00m) with 100mm dia PVC weep holes @ 1.20m c/c staggered in non-woven geotextile envelopes.
2. Internal Ground Reinforcement (LaRiMiT Cluster 5 / CEDD Geoguide 7):
   Prescribed Soil Nailing Array (Dia. 28 mm (Fe500 High-Yield Deformed Steel)) installed in 125 mm drillholes at 15° to 20° downward rake, 1.75 m (H) x 1.75 m (V) Staggered Pattern, length 10.0 m to 14.0 m, neat cementitious grout (f_cu >= 30 MPa) with 2% sacrificial pullout verification testing.
3. Hydrogeological Pore-Pressure Depression (LaRiMiT Cluster 3 / CEDD TGN 24):
   Subsurface Directional Drainage Array: 15.0 m per borehole (Total 5 Nos. array) slotted PVC pipes (O90 geotextile filter sock) installed at 5° to 10° upward rake for gravity self-cleansing flow to discharge perched groundwater, supplemented by lined crest interceptor catch drains (0.84 m x 0.61 m) and hillside saucer channels.
4. Dynamic Rockfall / Debris Barrier (LaRiMiT Cluster 6 / CEDD GEO Report 138):
   Installation of 3000 kJ Rating flexible ring net barrier (H=5.0 m, HEB 220 Structural Steel Section) with energy dissipators along active fall chutes.
5. Nature-Based Solutions & Bioengineering (LaRiMiT Cluster 8):
   Deep-Rooting Vetiver Grass Contour Hedges (Chrysopogon zizanioides) and coir geotextile bio-turfing (700 GSM) across reprofiled slope faces to restore matric suction and prevent shallow surficial raveling.
ai_assessment.other_observations: Sub-surface groundwater seepage daylighting along the colluvial mantle and Phyllite bedrock interface, confirming elevated perched phreatic levels during rainfall. Active extensional tension fissures (apertures 15-45 mm) trace 8-15 m uphill of the detachment crown. Relict discontinuity set J1 (53° dip daylighting adversely into the slope face) exhibits planar persistent slickensides with iron-oxide staining, confirming kinematic daylighting and high susceptibility to progressive retrogressive failure during prolonged monsoon precipitation.

safety_directives.permanent_restoration: Construction of a reinforced concrete breast wall with deep-seated soil nailing and systematic drainage improvement.

ai_assessment.synthesis_remarks:
1. GEOTECHNICAL & USGS CLASSIFICATION (USGS Circular 1325 / Cruden & Varnes 1996):
Forensic field reconnaissance of the Mandi sector confirms an active mass wasting event conforming strictly to the USGS standard definition of a landslide: "A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement."
Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) two-term taxonomy, the failure is formally designated as: Translational Rock Slide (Rock Block Slide) (Kinematic Movement: Translational Slide, Substrate: Rock, Velocity Rating: Rapid [Class 5, 1.8 m/h to 3 m/min]).

2. CONSEQUENCE RATING & TARGET FACTOR OF SAFETY (CEDD Geoguide 1):
Directly impacting mandi sub-divisional hill road corridor. Under Hong Kong CEDD Geoguide 1 criteria, the slope is classified as Category 2 (Moderate Consequence), requiring a statutory minimum target Factor of Safety FOS >= 1.25 under 10-year return period rainfall (FOS >= 1.15 under extreme storm conditions).

3. KINEMATIC FAILURE MECHANICS, ANATOMY & HYDROGEOLOGY:
Instability is characterized by A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults). within Phyllite strata under steep cut geometry (55° to 59° (Moderately Stable Cut)). Diagnostic landslide anatomical features (USGS Circular 1325) include an exposed detachment main scarp and depletion mass, open tension crown fissures, and an accumulation toe encroaching upon the corridor. Failure was triggered by antecedent rainfall infiltration inducing transient perched groundwater tables, loss of matric suction in the upper colluvium, and hydrostatic cleft-water pressure along daylighting relict joints (dipping 53° into the cut face).

4. MULTI-BARRIER MITIGATION STRATEGY (LaRiMiT / CEDD GEO Standards):
- Primary Toe Retention (LaRiMiT Cluster 4): Construction of a 13m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H=2.0m, Base B=1.00m) founded on competent bedrock with 100mm PVC weep holes @ 1.2m c/c.
- Internal Ground Reinforcement (LaRiMiT Cluster 5 / CEDD Geoguide 7): Prescribed Soil Nailing Array (Dia. 25 mm (Fe500 High-Yield Deformed Steel), 2.25 m (H) x 2.25 m (V) Square Pattern, length 6.0 m to 9.0 m) with sacrificial pullout verification testing.
- Pore Pressure Relief (LaRiMiT Cluster 3 / CEDD TGN 24): Installation of 15.0 m per borehole (Total 4 Nos. array) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains inclined at 5° to 10° upward rake for gravity self-cleansing flow to intercept perched seepage, paired with lined crest interceptor drains (0.84 m x 0.61 m).
- Dynamic Impact & NBS Protection: 500 kJ Rating flexible ring net barrier (CEDD GEO Report No. 138 / EOTA EAD 340059-00-0106) in fall zones, combined with Live Vegetated Crib Wall / Timber Cribbing.

5. STATUTORY MAINTENANCE REGIME:
Mandatory Engineer Inspection for Maintenance (EIM) at Every 2 years for Category 1 slopes; every 5 years for Category 2/3 slopes by a Qualified Geotechnical Engineer (Executive / Assistant Engineer) in strict accordance with CEDD Geoguide 5.

plain_language_explanation.summary_title: Active Slope Failure and Roadway Undermining
plain_language_explanation.what_happened: A significant portion of the hillside has detached, causing a landslide that has undermined the road structure.
plain_language_explanation.why_it_happened: The failure is driven by the weak, foliated nature of the local phyllite rock, exacerbated by water infiltration and poor drainage.
plain_language_explanation.property_and_access_impact: The road is partially blocked and structurally compromised, posing a risk of further collapse.
plain_language_explanation.road_and_travel_impact: Passage is obstructed (3.80 m (Single-Lane Traffic Operable)). Vehicles and pedestrians cannot safely transit this point.
plain_language_explanation.ongoing_hazards: Risk of secondary rockfalls and further subsidence of the road pavement.
plain_language_explanation.what_needs_to_be_done: Immediate debris removal, installation of temporary shoring, and long-term slope stabilization using soil nails and drainage.
plain_language_explanation.citizen_safety_advice: Avoid the area, do not park vehicles near the scarp, and follow all traffic diversions.

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: A hard or firm mass that was intact and in its natural place before the initiation of movement.
usgs_classification.movement_definition: Spatially continuous movement in which shear surfaces are short-lived, closely spaced, and usually not preserved; component velocities resemble those in a viscous fluid.

velocity_class.consequences: Loss of life expected; some temporary evacuation possible; structures destroyed.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.standard_reference: USGS Circular 1325 (Highland & Bobrowsky, 2008) & Cruden & Varnes (1996) TRB Special Report 247

cedd_consequence.consequence_criteria: Secondary roads (State Highways, Major District Roads), bus stands, open commercial yards, rural bypasses where failure causes severe transit disruption but low direct risk to occupied buildings.
cedd_consequence.mandatory_investigation: Engineer Inspection for Maintenance (EIM) & Preventive Upgrading

nature_based_solution.description: Dense linear vegetative hedges with 2-3m deep massive fibrous root systems (tensile strength ~75 MPa) providing mechanical soil binding and hydraulic shear enhancement.

flexible_barrier.debris_clearance: 0.5m to 0.8m bottom clearance for water and fluid slurry passage while retaining coarse boulder fronts

subsurface_drainage.pipe_specification: 50mm to 75mm dia heavy-duty slotted PVC pipe (Schedule 80)
subsurface_drainage.slot_aperture: 1.0mm to 1.5mm transverse slots @ 10mm c/c with 15% open drainage area
subsurface_drainage.filter_sock: Non-woven needle-punched polypropylene geotextile sock (O90 < 0.15mm) to prevent silt piping
subsurface_drainage.upward_inclination: 5° to 10° upward rake for gravity self-cleansing flow
subsurface_drainage.array_spacing: 3.0 m to 6.0 m c/c staggered across slope face or wall base

boq_items.description: Slope trimming, scarp reprofiling, and dressing of unstable overburden cut face to stable bench profile in all kinds of soil and soft rock.
boq_items.short_description: Slope trimming, scarp reprofiling & bench dressing in overburden cut face

boq_items.description: Foundation trench excavation in hard rock / compact boulder strata with pneumatic breaker tools, including necessary shoring, strutting, and dewatering for breast wall footing.
boq_items.short_description: Foundation trench rock excavation with pneumatic breaker tools for wall footing

boq_items.description: Construction of Plum Concrete Retaining / Breast Wall (H=3.7m, B=1.85m, b=0.60m) in M15 grade concrete (1:2:4) with 30% to 40% clean sound quarry plum boulders (density >= 18 kN/m³), including steel shuttering, scaffolding, compaction, and 14 days water curing.

boq_items.description: Supplying and laying non-woven needle-punched polypropylene geotextile filter fabric (weight >= 250 GSM, O90 < 0.15 mm) behind retaining wall backface.
boq_items.short_description: Non-woven needle-punched polypropylene geotextile filter fabric (250 GSM)

boq_items.description: Providing and laying free-draining granular backfill filter material (crushed stone gravel 20-40mm) behind retaining wall in layers not exceeding 150mm compacted thickness.
boq_items.short_description: Free-draining granular filter backfill material (20-40mm crushed gravel)

boq_items.description: Providing and installing 100mm dia heavy-duty PVC weep hole pipes (Class 3) placed at 1.20m c/c staggered with 1:20 outward slope and gravel filter envelope at inlet (Total 50 Nos.).
boq_items.short_description: 100mm dia PVC weep hole pipes @ 1.2m c/c staggered with gravel filter inlet

boq_items.short_description: Drilling 100-110mm dia boreholes for soil nails at 15°-20° rake (19 Nos. x 10.0m)

boq_items.short_description: Dia 28mm Fe500 high-yield steel soil nail bars with centralizers @ 2m c/c

boq_items.short_description: Pressure grouting of boreholes with non-shrink cementitious grout (>=30 MPa)
